title: Scoped Service Token Issuance and Audit Playbook
author: Maya Alvarez
content:
Overview
========

Purpose
-------
This playbook defines how Redwood issues, manages, audits, and evidences scoped short-lived service tokens (SSTs) used for service-to-service authentication across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. It focuses on minimizing blast radius, ensuring audit fidelity, supporting regulatory evidence collection, and integrating with incident response and exception workflows.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all machine-to-machine credentials issued by Redwood central token service (token-redwood-svc) and by sanctioned customer-controlled token brokers used in Private deployments.
- Covers issuance, signing, rotation, revocation, audit instrumentation, log retention/residency requirements, compliance packaging, and risk exception handling.
- Excludes long lived human API keys; those are handled by the developer-keys policy.

Definitions
-----------
- Scoped Service Token (SST): A short-lived JWT or opaque token limited to an explicit set of capabilities (scopes).
- Token Broker: Component that mints SSTs on behalf of a workload after authenticating the requestor. Examples: token-redwood-svc, vpc-broker.
- Evidence Bundle: Structured archive (JSON + signed manifest) used to satisfy audit requests.

Ownership and Roles
-------------------
- Security team: policy owner, audit schema definition, compliance packaging.
- Identity & Access (I&A) infra: implements token brokers, signing key rotation automation, and audit enrichment hooks.
- SRE / Platform: ensures audit log ingestion SLOs and alerting on token anomalies.
- App owners: declare required scopes, TTL tolerances, and emergency contacts.

High-level Principles
---------------------
1. Least privilege by default: tokens must express minimum scopes and shortest practical TTL.
2. Strong auditability: every issuance and revocation event must emit a canonical audit event with correlation metadata.
3. Tamper-evident evidence: retention-ready manifests and signed digests allow reconstruction for regulatory requests.
4. Automated rotation and emergency revoke: no manual key-handling for standard flows.

Token Configuration Standard (example table)
-------------------------------------------
| Field | Requirement | Default / Allowed | Owner |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| token_type | jwt | jwt | I&A infra |
| signing_alg | RS256 or PS256 | RS256 | I&A infra |
| scope | explicit resource:action strings | no wildcard allowed | App owner |
| ttl | seconds | 300–86400 (5m to 24h) default 3600 | App owner + Security approval for >24h |
| audience | service_id | must match target svc | App owner |
| issued_by | token broker id | token-redwood-svc | I&A infra |
| rotate_window | seconds before expiry to refresh | 0.5 * ttl recommended | I&A infra |
| key_id | signing key id | rotated daily for KMS keys | I&A infra |

Issuance Flow (step-by-step)
----------------------------
1. Requesting workload authenticates to the Token Broker using mTLS or platform identity (OIDC assertion) and presents the intended scope request.
2. Broker validates caller identity, enrollment status, and policy (including deny-lists and region residency constraints).
3. Broker performs policy evaluation and logs a pre-issue event containing request_id, caller_id, requested_scopes, policy_decision, and region_hint.
4. If approved, broker mints SST, attaches metadata header (key_id, issued_at, ttl, correlation_id), and returns token. The mint event is logged as an issuance event.
5. Client must persist correlation_id for future revoke/forensics workflows.

Audit Event Schema (canonical fields, JSON example)
--------------------------------------------------
- event_type: issuance | pre-issue | revoke | auto-rotate | validation-failure
- event_time: RFC3339 timestamp
- event_id: UUID
- actor: service or principal id
- target: token (kid / token hash partial), audience, scope list
- request_id: correlation id generated by broker
- decision: allow | deny | escalate
- region_hint: region code
- evidence_refs: list of evidence manifest ids

JSON example (shortened)
```
{\n  "event_type": "issuance",\n  "event_time": "2026-01-12T14:22:10Z",\n  "event_id": "9f14a3f2-2b6d-4c3a-b2e3-0a8f7d2c1e4a",\n  "actor": "svc-frontdoor-1.prod",\n  "target": {"kid": "key-20260112-12", "aud": "svc-backend-42"},\n  "request_id": "req-6f9b3a",\n  "decision": "allow",\n  "region_hint": "us-west-2",\n  "evidence_refs": ["evidence-20260112-req6f9b3a"]\n}\n```

Audit Logging Requirements
--------------------------
- All issuance/revoke/validation-failure events MUST be emitted to the central audit log stream.
- SLO: ingest to central system within 3 minutes for 99.9% of events; alert if pipeline lag > 5 minutes for >= 5 minutes.
- Logs must include partial token digests (first and last 8 hex chars) rather than full token values to avoid unnecessary exposure while enabling forensic correlation.
- Logs must include tenant_id, region, broker_id, and correlation_id.
- For Private deployments with customer-managed residency constraints, an event mirror must be maintained locally and a digest-only stub sent to central system if cross-border transfer is restricted.

Retention and Data Residency Guidance
------------------------------------
- Retention baseline: issuance/revoke events retained for 7 years for accounts with enterprise contracts; default retention 1 year for standard accounts.
- Sensitive tenants (regulated): evidence bundles preserved for contractual term + 3 years.
- When cross-border restrictions apply: keep full events in-region and publish signed digests to central compliance index. The digest must be sufficient to prove event existence and order but not contain PII.
- Archive format: gzipped JSONL + signed manifest (SHA256) stored in immutable object storage with WORM capability.

Evidence Bundle Contents (minimum)
---------------------------------
- manifest.json (signed by security-signing key)
- issuance-events.jsonl (canonical events for the period)
- broker-config.yaml (token policy snapshot)
- key-rotation-log.csv (keys used and time ranges)
- policy-decision-exports.json
- chain-of-custody.txt (who packaged, timestamp, package checksum)

Compliance Packaging: steps to produce an Evidence Bundle
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Query central audit store for all events matching correlation_id(s) and time window.
2. Include broker config snapshot as-of issuance time.
3. Export signing key metadata (key ids, rotation timestamps) — do not include private key material.
4. Produce manifest.json listing file names, sizes, and SHA256 digests.
5. Security signs the manifest using the security-signing key and uploads bundle to the compliance S3 bucket.
6. Register evidence id in evidence registry with retention policy and linked legal hold flags if required.

Runbook: Emergency Revoke (fast path)
------------------------------------
Purpose: immediate containment for suspected compromise.
Trigger: detection of anomalous token use, key compromise, or confirmed breach.
Steps:
1. SRE or Security runbook owner opens incident and adds legal/PR contacts.
2. Use the token-redwood-svc revoke API with correlation_id or token_digest as primary identifiers:
   - CLI example: token-redwoodctl revoke --digest "aa11ff...cc22" --reason "suspected-exfil"
3. Broker emits revoke event (must include incident_id).
4. Propagate revoke to edge caches and API gateways: force cache-bust and reject previously accepted tokens based on token digest or revocation list.
5. Produce evidence bundle for window T0-48h->T0+48h and mark as high-priority in evidence registry.
6. If signing key suspected, rotate signing key immediately using automated KMS flow and produce key-rotation log entry.
7. Post-mortem: collect issuance/revoke/validation logs, validate detection rules, and update deny-lists and policies.

Exception and Risk Acceptance Process
------------------------------------
- Request for non-standard token TTL or wildcard scope must be submitted via the Access Exception workflow with the following fields: owner, justification, risk-mitigation, compensating controls, expiry date.
- Security reviews exceptions, assigns a risk tier and mitigation steps, and issues a timebound approval if accepted.
- All exceptions are recorded in the exception register with evidence items attached. Exceptions for service tokens beyond 90 days require VP-level signoff.

Monitoring, Detection, and Alerting
----------------------------------
- Key signals to monitor:
  - Unusual issuance volume by principal or IP
  - High revoke frequency for a principal
  - Validation failures across regions
  - Issuance requests from unmanaged brokers
- Alerts: critical for cross-tenant anomalous issuance and for KMS key rotation failures.
- Weekly dashboard: top 10 callers by issuance count, top 10 scopes by volume, 90th/95th/99th percentile TTLs requested.

Developer & Operator Guidance
----------------------------
- App owners should declare required scopes in service manifests (service.yaml) and request longer TTLs only after load testing.
- Use SDK helper functions to obtain and cache SSTs with early-refresh: refresh at 50% ttl or on 401/invalid token.
- Avoid embedding tokens in logs. If unavoidable, redact and emit token digest only.

Examples and CLI snippets
------------------------
Minting request (curl)
```
curl -X POST https://token-broker.redwood.internal/v1/mint \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <platform-assertion>" \
  -d '{"aud":"svc-backend-42", "scope":["write:orders"], "ttl":3600}'
```
Revoke example (CLI)
```
token-redwoodctl revoke --digest "a1b2c3...f9e8" --incident "INC-20260112-45"
```

Compliance QA Checklist (pre-release)
-------------------------------------
- [ ] Policy rules for requested scopes exist and have test coverage.
- [ ] Audit events emitted for pre-issue, issuance, validation-failure, revoke.
- [ ] Evidence bundle generation validated end-to-end in staging.
- [ ] Retention and residency knobs configured for tenant.
- [ ] Automated key rotation timing tested with no more than 30s signing gap in rolling rotation.

Appendix: Token Broker Policy Decision Matrix (condensed)
-------------------------------------------------------
- If caller is platform-enrolled AND scope is read-only AND ttl <= 1h -> allow automated issuance.
- If caller is non-enrolled OR requested wildcard scope -> deny and escalate to manual approval.
- If caller requests cross-region audience where tenant residency disallows -> deny and produce digest-only event.

End of document
